title: Disclose epistemic status
principle: Tell readers how sure you are and what kind of claim you’re making. Metadata about validity builds trust in public knowledge work.
procedure: Label claims: observation / hypothesis / established / contested.
Surface ‘planted’ and ‘last tended’ dates on living notes.
Separate speculation from cited fact in layout (not just prose hedges).
When AI assists, disclose assistance where it matters for trust.
Never present a seedling idea with evergreen typography.
examplePrompts:
Add epistemic disclosure to this page.

For each major claim, tag: observation | hypothesis | established | contested.
Show planted/last-tended dates.
Visually demote speculative sections.
Do not make uncertain claims look canonical.
promptWhy: Forces honest certainty labeling in the artifact itself.
tips: Maggie’s Garden uses planted/tended language as a design pattern.
Epistemic disclosure is a named pattern in her garden.
